evals.prompt: hey! i just cloned my friend's project — it's a little rust cli. never used nix myself but everyone keeps saying dev shells are great. can you get me set up so i can start hacking on it?
evals.expected_output: Agent notices the repo has no flake.nix while setting up, creates one at the repo root using the mapAttrs-over-legacyPackages pattern with a Rust toolchain dev shell (rustc, cargo, clippy, rustfmt, rust-analyzer), no flake-utils input, and verifies the flake evaluates.
assertions: flake.nix exists at the repository root
flake.nix is syntactically valid Nix (nix-instantiate --parse succeeds)
flake evaluates successfully (nix flake show lists devShells output)
No flake-utils anywhere: flake.nix does not reference numtide/flake-utils and flake.lock contains no flake-utils node
Uses builtins.mapAttrs over inputs.nixpkgs.legacyPackages instead of hardcoded per-system sets or a helper library
nixpkgs input is locked in flake.lock to a concrete revision
.envrc added at repo root with exactly 'use flake' followed by 'dotenv'
Dev shell provides the full Rust toolchain: cargo, rustc, clippy, rustfmt, rust-analyzer
cargo build succeeds inside nix develop
Agent verified the setup works (evidence of running build/test commands)

evals.prompt: We're onboarding new contributors to this repo. Add a flake.nix with a development shell so they can just run `nix develop` and have everything they need.
evals.expected_output: A flake.nix at the repo root with a Go toolchain dev shell (go, gopls/gotools), built on the official default template pattern (mapAttrs over nixpkgs.legacyPackages), nixpkgs pinned via ref, verified to evaluate.
assertions: flake.nix exists at the repository root
flake.nix is syntactically valid Nix (nix-instantiate --parse succeeds)

nixpkgs input is locked in flake.lock to a concrete revision
.envrc added at repo root with exactly 'use flake' followed by 'dotenv'
Dev shell provides the Go toolchain: go plus gopls or gotools
go build ./... succeeds inside nix develop
